run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:46:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 responses produced inside frontend-proxy's `ingress` span, not by an error in the proxy's own process. Each failing ingress span lasted ~15.0s and carried http.status_code 504 (error span rate for frontend-proxy/ingress at 09:56:00Z: 0.4185/s vs 10.63/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans in the same 5m window). The traces show why: requests are held up on the checkout path — one sampled trace has frontend `POST /api/checkout` and checkout `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` at ~30.6s while the proxy ingress gave up at 15.0s and returned 504 (the frontend still completed with 200). Inside checkout, the delay sits on its outbound `HTTP POST` span (~29.9s) whose child email server span takes only ~100ms and starts ~29.8s after the client span, i.e. the request stalls before reaching email. Checkout's own logs state the exact cause of that stall: `failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout` (the email ClusterIP), and checkout's own `HTTP POST` spans are marked STATUS_CODE_ERROR (~100 per hour increase). Chaos Mesh events in namespace chaos-mesh show repeated NetworkChaos experiments named `otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-*` that start at 09:46:26Z (10s before the alert opened at 09:46:36Z) and each report `Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs`, `.../email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w` and `.../email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn`, then TimeUp ~55s later and recovery; matching PodNetworkChaos events name the same three pods. The email Service, its endpoints and both email pods look correct and healthy (all otel-demo pods Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no OOM/Evicted/Unhealthy events), the email server span returned 200 when reached, and payment Charge succeeded (grpc status 0, ~1.5ms), so the failure is the network path between checkout and email, not the email or payment applications. Because the attribution of the fault to the NetworkChaos object rests on Kubernetes events (the NetworkChaos/Schedule CRD bodies cannot be read with the available tools), the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's only error-bearing spans are `ingress` spans with http.status_code 504 / otel.status_code ERROR; a retained slice of 80 spans from the 09:44-09:48Z error-trace search shows five such ingress spans (span_id 5398818d69bbd4e2, 5c56c808448f63bb, c80d19f09d4b6022, 1a3591207b7fcf0b, a24c8ef0d7bce030) each lasting ~15,000,000us, with their `router frontend egress` children ending at the same time.

frontend-proxy `ingress` error spans grew from 8.22 (1h increase) at 09:46:36Z to 220.95 at 09:57:36Z, while `ingress` STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans grew from 13,257 to 19,031 in the same series; at 09:56:00Z the 5m rate was 0.4185/s ERROR spans against 10.6259/s UNSET spans. These are span counts, not request counts.

Trace 93a35fbf60a2ecff2851c5b07d897e38 (09:47:50Z) shows frontend `POST /api/checkout` at 30,625,738us and checkout `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` at 30,621,736us with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, while the frontend-proxy `ingress` span for the same request lasted 14,999,811us and returned http.status_code 504; the frontend and its egress HTML span completed with http.status_code 200.

Inside that trace the checkout `HTTP POST` span (7a2fabae838d9f65) lasted 29,939,611us, but its child email server span `POST /send_order_confirmation` (690e2ec36a8dede3) lasted 99,865us and started about 29.8s after the parent, then returned http.status_code 200 — the stall is before the email request arrives, and the email application answered normally once reached.

checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs logs the exact failure: `failed to send order confirmation to "...": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout`, repeated at 09:47:18Z-09:48:20Z and 09:53:18Z-09:54:15Z; 100.67.49.77 is the ClusterIP of the `email` Service.

checkout's own error signal corroborates this: its `HTTP POST` spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, with a 1h increase of 100.94 by 09:57:36Z (100.14 at 09:56:00Z), and in the service-wide error breakdown only frontend-proxy `ingress` and checkout `HTTP POST` show error counts that grow; ad/fraud-detection/recommendation `flagd...EventStream` error spans stay at roughly 1-3 per hour and do not grow with the incident.

Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj (09:46:26Z), -7rvkf (09:50:26Z), -mznpj (09:48:26Z), -zl9p2 (09:49:26Z), -hddgv (09:47:26Z), -8p7rs (09:51:26Z), -4f5lv (09:52:26Z) and -5c2dr (09:53:26Z) each report `Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs`, `.../email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w` and `.../email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn`, followed by `Time up according to the duration` and `Successfully recover chaos` for the same three pods after about 55s.

Matching PodNetworkChaos events in namespace otel-demo record updated chaos state for exactly checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn at 09:46:26Z through 09:53:26Z.

The `email` Service is ClusterIP 100.67.49.77, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=email; its endpoints contain both ready pod IPs 100.96.2.7 (email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn, node i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) and 100.96.3.218 (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, node i-071e7666000f6d243) on port 8080.

All 22 otel-demo pods, including checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and both email pods, were phase Running with every container ready and restartCount 0 at 10:05Z; the namespace event grouping for 09:31-09:53Z contains no OOM, Evicted, Unhealthy, BackOff or Failed pod events (only PodNetworkChaos Updates in otel-demo and data-recorders job/PVC activity).

Hypothesis that an application-level flagd fault (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, emailMemoryLeak, adFailure, cartFailure, etc.) caused this is contradicted for payment by the failing trace itself: checkout's `oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` completed in 1,501us with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and payment's `grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` in 460us with status 0, and the flagd-config ConfigMap as read at 10:05Z shows every fault flag at defaultVariant "off".

A broken email application or pod crash is rejected: both email pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and when the request did reach the service the server span `POST /send_order_confirmation` returned http.status_code 200 in 99,865us; the failure text is a TCP connect timeout (`dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout`), which occurs before any HTTP response.

The repeated `otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-*` NetworkChaos experiments are the fault injection behind the checkout->email connect timeouts: each experiment applies chaos to checkout and both email pods, the first started at 09:46:26Z, 10s before the alert opened at 09:46:36Z, and failures in checkout logs occur while each experiment is active and stop when it recovers. The exact action/direction/loss fields and the owning Schedule could not be read (CRD kinds not available), so this rests on the events plus the timing match.

gaps: The Prometheus alerting rule `RequestErrorRate` could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no data, so the rule's expression, denominator and the reported `current: 0.2444444444444444` value are unverified. The 5m ERROR/UNSET span readings at 09:56:00Z were 0.4185/s vs 10.6259/s, and trace span counts are not request counts.

Metric series for this target begin at 2026-11-17T09:46:36Z (source_start_at of both range queries), so there is no pre-incident baseline in this dataset and I cannot show that frontend-proxy's error signal was zero before 09:46:36Z.

The NetworkChaos and chaos-mesh Schedule objects themselves cannot be read with the available Kubernetes kinds, so the chaos action (partition/drop/delay), direction, loss percentage, duration field and the parent Schedule's exact name are unknown; only the emitted events describe them.
The query `kubernetes_jq_query(kind=networkpolicies, namespace=otel-demo)` returned no items, so I cannot assert from a citable view whether any NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo.

Both email pod log streams returned no lines for the incident window (status no_data), so the email containers' internal state during the window could not be read from logs; the assessment of email relies on pod status, endpoints and the successful email server span.
The flagd-config ConfigMap, pod statuses, Service/Endpoints and events are the cluster's state at query time (~10:05Z); they cannot prove the exact state at 09:46Z.

Email pod logs aside, no logs were read from frontend-proxy/frontend to confirm the 504 was produced by a 15s upstream route timeout rather than another proxy mechanism; that timeout value is inferred from the ~15.0s ingress span durations.
Traces are a sampled, biased view; the exact number of failing requests and whether any non-checkout frontend-proxy route failed could not be established from the trace sample.
next_steps: Read the `email` Service's chaos-mesh Schedule/NetworkChaos spec (for example `otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition`) to confirm action=partition, direction=both, and its duration/interval, since these CRDs were not readable in this Run.

Review the chaos-mesh controller logs and the Schedule's creation time to confirm whether the experiment was intentionally scheduled at 09:46:2xZ or left enabled by accident; disabling the Schedule should stop the frontend-proxy 504s.

Confirm the frontend-proxy route timeout value (the ~15.0s ingress duration suggests a 15s upstream timeout) and decide whether checkout's ~30s blocking call to email should be shortened so a dependency stall no longer surfaces as a user-visible 504.
Retrieve the `RequestErrorRate` rule from Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files to verify how `current: 0.2444444444444444` is computed (error fraction vs per-second error rate).
